title: Google's Gemini Hits 950 Million Users as Alphabet Posts Blockbuster Q2 Earnings
excerpt: The AI chatbot is closing in on ChatGPT's billion-user mark while Alphabet's cloud revenue surges 82 percent, though a massive capex hike rattled investors.
body:
• Google's Gemini app reached 950 million monthly active users, up from 400 million a year ago, putting it within striking distance of ChatGPT.
  • Alphabet reported Q2 revenue of $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year, with cloud revenue surging 82% to $24.8 billion.
  • The company raised its capital expenditure guidance to $195–$205 billion for 2026, sending shares lower in after-hours trading.
  • CEO Sundar Pichai confirmed early work has begun on Gemini 4, Google's next-generation AI model.

Gemini's Rapid Ascent

Google's Gemini chatbot is on the cusp of joining the billion-user club. The AI assistant now has 950 million monthly active users, CEO Sundar Pichai revealed during Alphabet's second-quarter earnings call on July 22, with daily active users tripling over the past year.

https://x.com/Androidheadline/status/2080328346160747000

The growth trajectory has been steep. Gemini had 400 million monthly users when Pichai last reported figures at Google I/O in May 2025. That number climbed to 650 million by October, 750 million by February, and 900 million by this May's I/O keynote. Recent Sensor Tower data pegs rival ChatGPT at roughly one billion monthly users, making the gap between the two AI assistants the narrowest it has ever been.

"Our AI investments are redefining what's possible across every part of our business."

— Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet

New features such as Daily Brief and the personalised Gemini Spark assistant, now available in the US and several international markets, have fuelled adoption. Google's AI-powered Search products are also growing fast — AI Mode has crossed one billion monthly active users since its broader rollout last October, while AI Overviews serves more than 2.5 billion users monthly.

Record Cloud Growth Anchors Earnings Beat

Alphabet's overall results were strong. Revenue rose 24 percent year-over-year to $119.8 billion, beating analyst estimates of $116.9 billion. Earnings per share came in at $9.11, a 294 percent jump over the same period last year.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=3fJ0yv85fIA

The standout was Google Cloud, which posted $24.8 billion in revenue — an 82 percent increase driven by enterprise demand for AI infrastructure. The cloud backlog swelled to $514 billion, more than doubling from the prior quarter, according to the Wall Street Journal. Nearly 90 percent of Fortune 100 companies now use Gemini Enterprise.

On the developer side, more than nine million developers build applications monthly using Google's AI models, with the company's APIs processing around 22 billion tokens per minute, up from 16 billion in the prior quarter.

Investor Anxiety Over Spending

Despite the strong top line, Alphabet's stock fell more than four percent in after-hours trading before partially recovering. The trigger: a revised capital expenditure forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion for 2026, up from the previous $180–$190 billion range.

"You can't be offloading this much cash and not talk about it."

— Brian Mulberry, portfolio manager, Zacks Investment Management

Google reported $44.9 billion in capex for the second quarter alone. To help finance its data centre build-out, the company announced an $85 billion equity raise last month. Truist Securities analyst Youssef Squali warned the upper-end figure could push 2027 capex as high as $270–$280 billion.

The spending concern was compounded by competitive headwinds. Gemini 3.5 Pro, Google's flagship model, has been delayed due to shortcomings in coding and agentic tasks, Reuters reported. Meanwhile, Anthropic released its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models in June, and OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 this month. Google responded this week with three lighter models — Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber — though none replace the missing Pro upgrade.

The Road to a Billion

Pichai confirmed that pretraining has begun on Gemini 4, Google's next-generation model, and said he is "very excited" about its progress. The company's Antigravity AI coding tool has reached 2.4 million weekly active users, while YouTube saw 1.7 billion unique viewers watch World Cup content during the 2026 tournament.

For Google's vast user base in India — a market Pichai has personally championed since his days leading Chrome and Android — the expansion of Gemini Spark and AI Mode into international markets signals accelerated access to consumer AI features. India remains one of Google's largest user markets by volume, and the Gemini rollout there has been a key driver of the app's user growth.

Whether Gemini crosses the billion-user mark before year-end will depend on sustained product momentum and the competitive response from OpenAI and Anthropic. But with 950 million users and tripling engagement, Google is closer than most expected six months ago.
nri_angle: Indian-born CEO Sundar Pichai leads Google's AI transformation while India remains a key growth market for Gemini's expansion into international markets.
author: Diaspora Desk
